claims.text: Deliberately NOT a forest node id: functions are not forest nodes today (the forest's nodes are files and documents), so ``consumes``/``produces`` attach to the FILE node and carry this string in their attributes.
claims.why: No code in this chunk creates or uses 'consumes'/'produces' attributes; no forest node definition is present.

claims.text: Join it to a ``CodeUnit`` on ``(module, line)`` -- never on ``name``, which is a bare leaf and collapses ``Cls.emit`` onto ``emit``.
claims.why: No CodeUnit class or usage appears in this chunk.

claims.text: True for a ``type``/``field`` node id. For forest and dss guards.
claims.why: The function returns True iff node_id starts with 'type:' or 'field:', matching the docstring claim.

claims.text: The repo-root dotted namespace, for callers that have no ``_PyNaming``.
claims.why: _PyNaming is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: ``index.build_index`` passes its own ``_PyNaming`` (the authority: it knows about declared package roots and center-relative spellings). This is the no-center view, which is what an unconfigured repo gets anyway, and it exists so tools and tests can resolve without importing ``index`` -- which they must not do, because ``index`` imports THIS module.
claims.why: index module and its build_index function are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Only two members are used from either object, so they are interchangeable by duck typing: ``name(rel)`` and ``tables_for(rel).rel_by_dotted`` / ``.canon``.
claims.why: No usage of name() or tables_for() from an external object is shown; .canon is set to empty dict in from_rels.

claims.text: Mirrors index._disambiguate: a .pyi is a stub DECLARING its .py sibling, not a rival module; two genuine modules claiming one dotted name is a real ambiguity and is refused, not tie-broken.
claims.why: index._disambiguate not present in this chunk; logic here only uses .pyi exclusion and single-candidate tie-break.
The function strips .py suffix and replaces '/' with '.', matching the example.

claims.text: rel -> {qualname: TypeDecl}: THE table invariant I2 demands.
claims.why: Invariant I2 not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: It is never merged into ``graph.SymbolResolver.defs_by_file`` and never passed to ``graph.build_resolver``.
claims.why: graph module and its classes/functions not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Keyed by the full in-file ``qualname`` (``Outer.Inner``, not ``Inner``), because a leaf-name key would make two nested classes with the same leaf name collide and force a tie-break.
claims.why: No example of nested classes or leaf-name key usage shown; the function uses decl.qualname as key.

claims.text: A qualname declared twice in one file (an ``if``/``try`` pair) keeps the FIRST by line: both spellings share one node id, so there is nothing to arbitrate. The count is published as ``duplicate_declarations``.
claims.why: The function uses dict.setdefault, which keeps the first occurrence, matching 'keeps the FIRST by line'. However, 'the count is published as duplicate_declarations' is uncheckable because no such count is returned or stored in this function.

observations.what: types_by_file uses dict.setdefault to keep first decl, but docstring claims duplicate count is published; no such count in code.
PlainNaming.from_rels sets canon to empty dict; docstring says .canon is used, but it's never populated.
